# codebase-place-org

Browser-native workspace / virtual-desktop / local-first "place" lineage.
Donor of the Launchpad/HQ/Virtual-Desktop UX metaphor that resurfaces in the
fresh-context product framing. Not architectural; preserve as visual + spatial
intent only.

## Why this matters

Original Next.js implementation of the place.org virtual desktop. Read `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` for the agent-collaboration patterns the user has used; read `app/(desktop)/` for the UX scaffolding that the v1.1 Launchpad/HQ shell will replace or wrap.

## What lives here

- `code/place.org/AGENTS.md` — agent-collaboration conventions
- `code/place.org/CLAUDE.md` — Claude-specific working notes
- `code/place.org/README.md` — project README
- `code/place.org/app/(desktop)/layout.tsx`, `code/place.org/app/(desktop)/page.tsx` — desktop surface scaffolding
- (full Next.js app under `code/place.org/app/` — explore on demand)

## Where it connects

- Inspires: `codebase-place-companion`, `codebase-place-org-openclaw`, `docs-host-system-launchpad-hq`, `docs-vault-wiki`
- Concept donor for: every `ux-metaphor` topic node

## How to load it efficiently

```bash
git show origin/codebase-place-org:code/place.org/AGENTS.md
git show origin/codebase-place-org:code/place.org/app/'(desktop)'/layout.tsx
```

## Doctrine extracted (2026-04-22)

Carries forward (principles, not code):
- **Boot before surface** — the desktop never renders apps until an explicit `boot-desktop` event fires; a separate `BootSequence` component owns the gate (`code/place.org/app/(desktop)/page.tsx` `DesktopPage` `useEffect` + `if (!booted)` branch). EMA's daemon should refuse surface mounts until control-plane health is confirmed.
- **Capability detection is its own lifecycle step** — `useCapabilitiesDetect` and `requestPersistentStorage` are first-class effects sitting alongside data wiring, not buried in components (`code/place.org/app/(desktop)/page.tsx` `Desktop()` hook stack). EMA should expose runtime capability probes as named init steps, not implicit checks.
- **Optional native bridge with graceful fallback** — `companionBridge.connect()` is wired unconditionally and the sustained-use nudge only fires after real activity, never blocking the browser-only path (`code/place.org/app/(desktop)/page.tsx` `useCompanionBridge` + `useCompanionSustainedNudge`). EMA's host-affinity placement must degrade the same way: daemon-absent surfaces still work.
- **Trust runtime-shipped docs over training data** — `AGENTS.md` instructs every agent to read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing code (`code/place.org/AGENTS.md` "This is NOT the Next.js you know"). EMA's harness drivers should pin their own protocol docs and require agents to load them per-session.

Leaves behind (residue):
- The 30+ React hook composition in one `Desktop()` body (window manager, glass intensity, font weight, screensaver) — UX surface detail, not authority.
- The browser-side `serviceWorker` + share-target plumbing (`useShareReceiver`, `sw.js` registration).

Topic relevance: `surface`, `ux-metaphor`, `placement`, `doctrine`, `driver`.
